@lex_node @0xSpuddy (The vast majority of our learning is observational and statistical. In many cultures, babies/infants are basically not interacted with at all by adults, and yet they develop into normal intelligence and skill range infants entirely through observation.)

Sure, yes. My point is that LLMs learn in extremely alien ways to how humans learn, and—a point I think you'd very much agree with—we should not make the mistake of hewing too closely to human analogies in how they think/behave.

There are a lot of human priors, both in our DNA and our socialization, that LLMs don't have. They can ape them when told to. But they're not really there, and we don't know how to get them in there.

They are more like feral children who learn to behave around adults.

@richardartoul @udiWertheimer Let's say AIs that are better than 99%th percentile humans at producing knowledge and advancing the technological frontier.

One example: an international ban on COCONUT and fixed-width transformer models.

COCONUT style models, which instead of outputting tokens in their "CoT," they simply dump activations—inscrutable high-dimensional vectors—and feed those back into the next forward pass of the model. 

It's been shown that training a reasoning model COCONUT-style is more effective at certain types of problems, and probably does not lead to any loss in performance. (After all, rendering a token in the CoT is compressing a higher-dimensional distribution into a single value; keeping the distribution should lead to strictly better performance. It's intuitive why this is better. High-dimensional vectors are strictly more expressive than tokens.)

However, we have no idea wtf a COCONUT style model is doing. We cannot read its chain of thought. We know that it's thinking, but its CoT is completely invisible to us. It can be scheming, planning attacks, trying to deceive us, and we would have no trace of any such behavior.

This is very unsafe. We should not normalize this or wander down this alley. We should make sure we can always monitor reasoning models and that we DESPERATELY AVOID any kind of optimization pressure on the chain of thought. If chain of thought reasoning does not remain as veridical as possible, even if right now we don't think it's that dangerous to have a COCONUT model today, it could lead to catastrophic loss of control events down the road if we normalize this.

This is "slowdown" type stuff.

It means let's spend more time researching how to make sure that CoT remains monitorable and models stay veridical about their behavior, how to make them cheat less and reward hack less and so on.

But it's totally fine to spend that time doing mundane economic acceleration, like RL on accounting tasks, or obscure coding languages, or video generation (as Opus 5.5 seems to have). That is not implied by a "coordinated slowdown"

Agreed. economic growth is imperative. That said, existing frontier models have barely diffused into the economy/GDP numbers even today, so I doubt we are resuming to baseline. I think that's true even if training runs plateau for other reasons; just getting Astra/Opus 5.5 burnt into an ASIC and handing one to everyone will increase GDP massively.

If it's true that we can always adjust how this stuff behaves, why do you think hallucinations are still a thing? Clearly it's very bad for business that models sometimes hallucinate still. We've gotten hallucinations down, but nowhere near 0.

These are fundamentally stochastic systems, and we don't fully understand how they work. That's what the whole field of mechanistic interpretability is trying to tackle.

I got in touch with the team over at LimitBreak and they quickly paused Payment Processor V3, which was subject to the same exploit. Unfortunately, V2 was not pausable, so the only path towards protecting affected assets was to run a whitehat operation.

Similarly, V3 on ApeChain is temporarily in a state where it cannot be paused, so ApeChain assets approved to V3 needed to be saved as well.

All in all, we rescued 23,155 NFTs worth north of $5.7M USD.

We later discovered that a similar exploit could be used in reverse to steal WETH. 660 WETH was at risk, which we unfortunately were not fast enough to recover. Apologies to those affected.

Shout out to @Boomskite for flagging the initial exploit tx to me, and @coffeedev @0xjustadev and @whiteoakkong for acting quickly and assisting with the recovery.

All NFTs are safely relocated. Soon, owners will be able claim them back after revoking the exploitable approvals.

Addresses to revoke below.
